actions.justification: MANDATORY — deadline 10 minutes. Patient is critically ill with HR 128, BP 90/60, RR 34, SpO2 80%. Formal vital signs assessment is required per GOLD COPD guidelines as the first step in exacerbation assessment.

MANDATORY — absent breath sounds on the right and tracheal deviation to the left with severe hypoxia (SpO2 80%) must be formally assessed. Critical to differentiate tension pneumothorax (due to bullous emphysema) from COPD exacerbation before initiating NIV or oxygen therapy.

MANDATORY — chest X-ray is required per GOLD guidelines to confirm diagnosis. Essential to identify pneumothorax (given absent right breath sounds and tracheal deviation), which would contraindicate NIV and alter management entirely.
Mandatory action per GOLD COPD guidelines: ABG required to assess severity, hypercapnia, and acid-base status in severe exacerbation with SpO2 80% and RR 34.

Patient is critically ill with hypoxia (SpO2 80%), hypotension, and tachycardia. Mental status assessment is essential to guide NIV eligibility and urgency of intervention. Also, absent breath sounds on right with tracheal deviation raises concern for tension pneumothorax — mental status helps gauge urgency.

SpO2 is critically low at 80%. Controlled supplemental oxygen is needed immediately, titrating carefully to avoid worsening hypercapnia (Haldane effect) in this COPD/emphysema patient. Target SpO2 88-92%.
Mandatory per GOLD COPD guidelines for severe exacerbation; must be given within 30 minutes. Patient is at 30 minutes with severe hypoxia and hemodynamic instability requiring urgent bronchodilation.

Mandatory per GOLD COPD guidelines. However, critical note: the clinical picture of absent breath sounds on right with tracheal deviation to left strongly suggests tension pneumothorax, which is an absolute contraindication for NIV. Assessment must explicitly rule out pneumothorax before initiating NIV.

Urgent pulmonology and likely thoracic surgery consult needed given the clinical presentation suggesting tension pneumothorax (absent right breath sounds, tracheal deviation left, hemodynamic instability with bullous emphysema/COPD) requiring immediate expert evaluation and potential needle decompression.
Mandatory per GOLD COPD guidelines for severe exacerbation. Reduces airway inflammation and improves outcomes. Not yet administered.
Mandatory per GOLD COPD guidelines for severe exacerbation with signs of infection risk. Indicated given severity of presentation.
CBC will help evaluate for leukocytosis suggesting infection, anemia contributing to hypoxia, and guide antibiotic and supportive therapy decisions in this critically ill COPD patient.
